meta.description: Candidate Cherokee translations of the 20 new Week 3 logic items (data/week3_new_logic_items.json), produced by Claude directly in conversation. Same honesty caveat as week1_cherokee.json applies, more strongly: several of these items (De Morgan's laws, biconditionals, triple negation, quantifier-scope order) involve logical connectives -- 'or', 'if and only if', nested negation -- that I have even less confident command of in Cherokee than the simpler Week 1 set. translator_confidence is 'very low' for most items. Never treat as ground truth; translation_validation.human_reviewed is false throughout.

items.english_source: It is not the case that both Alice is home and Bob is home. Question: Alice is not home or Bob is not home.
items.cherokee_candidate_translation: ᎥᏝ ᏱᏂᎦᎵᏍᏗᎭ ᎢᏧᎳ ᎡᎵᏏ ᎠᎴ ᏆᏈ ᎦᏁᎸ ᏱᎨᏐᎢ. ᎡᎵᏏ ᎥᏝ ᎦᏁᎸ ᏱᎨᏐ, ᎠᎴᏬ ᏆᏈ ᎥᏝ ᎦᏁᎸ ᏱᎨᏐ.
items.translator_confidence: very low; 'not both...and' and 'or' connectives are outside my confident Cherokee vocabulary
items.label: entailed

items.english_source: It is not the case that Chris is sick or Dana is sick. Question: Chris is not sick and Dana is not sick.
items.cherokee_candidate_translation: ᎥᏝ ᏳᏢᎩ ᎩᎵᏏ ᎠᎴᏬ ᏕᎾ ᏳᏢᎩ. ᎩᎵᏏ ᎥᏝ ᏳᏢᎩ ᎠᎴ ᏕᎾ ᎥᏝ ᏳᏢᎩ.
items.translator_confidence: very low
items.label: entailed

items.english_source: Not all birds can fly. Question: No birds can fly.
items.cherokee_candidate_translation: ᎥᏝ ᏂᎦᏛ ᏥᏍᏉᏗ ᏗᎦᏃᎸᏗ. ᎥᏝ ᎦᎵᏍᎩᏂ ᏥᏍᏉᏗ ᏗᎦᏃᎸᏗ ᏱᎩ.
items.translator_confidence: low; 'not all' vs 'none' distinction is exactly the hard part to convey
items.label: unknown

items.english_source: It is not true that it is not true that Eve is not tired. Question: Eve is not tired.
items.cherokee_candidate_translation: ᎥᏝ ᏚᏳᎪᏛ ᏱᎩ ᎾᏍᎩ ᎥᏝ ᏚᏳᎪᏛ ᏱᎩ ᎾᏍᎩ ᏈᏫ ᎥᏝ ᏳᏓᏅᏬᎯᏍᏗ. ᏈᏫ ᎥᏝ ᏳᏓᏅᏬᎯᏍᏗ.
items.translator_confidence: very low; triple negation compounds the same difficulty as the Week 1 double-negation item
items.label: entailed

items.english_source: It is not the case that if Frank studies, he fails. Question: Frank studies and Frank does not fail.
items.cherokee_candidate_translation: ᎥᏝ ᏱᏂᎦᎵᏍᏗᎭ ᎢᏳᏃ ᏋᎩ ᎠᎴᏅᏗᏍᎨᏍᏗ, ᎠᏲᏢᎦ. ᏋᎩ ᎠᎴᏅᏗᏍᎦ ᎠᎴ ᎥᏝ ᎠᏲᏢᎦ.
items.translator_confidence: very low
items.label: entailed

items.english_source: Hannah passes the class if and only if she completes all assignments. Hannah completed all assignments. Question: Hannah passes the class.
items.cherokee_candidate_translation: ᎭᎾ ᎠᎦᏛᎦ ᎠᏕᎶᏆᏍᏗ ᎠᏗᎾᏓᏅᏗ ᏂᎦᏛ ᏗᎦᎸᏫᏍᏓᏁᏗ ᏳᎪᏙᏗ. ᎭᎾ ᏂᎦᏛ ᏗᎦᎸᏫᏍᏓᏁᏗ ᎤᎪᏙᏗᎢ. ᎭᎾ ᎠᎦᏛᎦ ᎠᏕᎶᏆᏍᏗ.
items.translator_confidence: very low; biconditional ('if and only if') is not something I have confident Cherokee for -- rendered loosely as a plain conditional-like structure
items.label: entailed

items.english_source: Ian wins the game if and only if he rolls a six. Ian does not roll a six. Question: Ian does not win the game.
items.cherokee_candidate_translation: ᏔᏂ ᎠᎵᏆ ᏓᎩᏍᏗ ᎠᏗᎾᏓᏅᏗ ᏆᏱ ᏳᎦᏘᏴ. ᏔᏂ ᎥᏝ ᏳᎦᏘᏴ ᏆᏱ. ᏔᏂ ᎥᏝ ᎠᎵᏆ ᏓᎩᏍᏗ.
items.translator_confidence: very low; same biconditional issue as cond2_01
items.label: entailed

items.english_source: If Jack wakes up early, he goes for a run. If Jack goes for a run, he feels energetic. Jack feels energetic. Question: Jack woke up early.
items.cherokee_candidate_translation: ᎢᏳᏃ ᏥᎩ ᎩᎬᏱ ᎠᏗᏙᎳᏗᏍᎨᏍᏗ, ᎠᏍᏆᎳᏂᏙᎭ. ᎢᏳᏃ ᏥᎩ ᎠᏍᏆᎳᏂᏙᎲᏍᎨᏍᏗ, ᎤᏓᏅᏬᎯᏍᏗ ᎠᎵᎮᎵᎦ. ᏥᎩ ᎤᏓᏅᏬᎯᏍᏗ ᎠᎵᎮᎵᎦ. ᏥᎩ ᎩᎬᏱ ᎤᏗᏙᎳᏓᏅᎩ.
items.translator_confidence: very low
items.label: unknown

items.english_source: If Kim studies, she understands the material. If she understands the material, she passes the test. If she passes the test, she gets a certificate. Kim studies. Question: Kim gets a certificate.
items.cherokee_candidate_translation: ᎢᏳᏃ ᎩᎻ ᎠᎴᏅᏗᏍᎨᏍᏗ, ᎠᏬᎵᎦ. ᎢᏳᏃ ᎠᏬᎵᎲᏍᎨᏍᏗ, ᎠᎦᏙᎲᏍᎦ. ᎢᏳᏃ ᎠᎦᏙᎲᏍᎨᏍᏗ, ᎤᏂᏨᏗ ᏓᏥᏰᎲᏍᎦ. ᎩᎻ ᎠᎴᏅᏗᏍᎦ. ᎩᎻ ᏓᏥᏰᎲᏍᎦ ᎤᏂᏨᏗ.
items.translator_confidence: very low
items.label: entailed

items.english_source: Either Liam takes the train or he drives. Liam does not take the train. Question: Liam drives.
items.cherokee_candidate_translation: ᎳᎻ ᎤᎩᏍᏗᏍᎩ ᎠᏓᎦᏘᎸᏍᎩ ᎠᎴᏬ ᎤᏔᎾ ᎡᎬᏔᏂᏍᎬᎢ. ᎳᎻ ᎥᏝ ᏳᎩᏍᏗᏎ ᎠᏓᎦᏘᎸᏍᎩ. ᎳᎻ ᎤᏔᎾ ᎠᎬᏔᏂᏍᎦ.
items.translator_confidence: very low; 'either...or' disjunction is one of my weakest areas
items.label: entailed

items.english_source: All squares are rectangles. Question: All rectangles are squares.
items.cherokee_candidate_translation: ᏂᎦᏛ ᏅᎩᎦᏙᎯ ᏗᏂᎵᏍᏗ ᎾᏂᎳᏍᏗ ᎨᏐᎢ. ᏂᎦᏛ ᎾᏂᎳᏍᏗ ᏅᎩᎦᏙᎯ ᏗᏂᎵᏍᏗ ᎨᏐᎢ.
items.translator_confidence: low
items.label: unknown

items.english_source: All unicorns are magical. Question: Some unicorn is magical.
items.cherokee_candidate_translation: ᏂᎦᏛ ᏐᏉ ᎠᏰᏳᏍᏗ ᏐᏢᏗ ᎤᏂᎭ ᎨᏐᎢ. ᎢᎦᏛ ᏐᏉ ᎠᏰᏳᏍᏗ ᏐᏢᏗ ᎠᎭ.
items.translator_confidence: very low
items.label: unknown

items.english_source: All mammals are animals. All dogs are mammals. Question: All dogs are animals.
items.cherokee_candidate_translation: ᏂᎦᏛ ᏗᏥᏍᏛ ᎠᏰᎵ ᏗᏂᏱᏍᎩ ᎨᏐᎢ. ᏂᎦᏛ ᎩᏟ ᏗᏥᏍᏛ ᎨᏐᎢ. ᏂᎦᏛ ᎩᏟ ᏗᏂᏱᏍᎩ ᎨᏐᎢ.
items.translator_confidence: low; 'mammal' and 'animal' as distinct category words are uncertain
items.label: entailed

items.english_source: Every student has a favorite teacher. Question: There is a teacher who is every student's favorite.
items.cherokee_candidate_translation: ᏂᎦᏛ ᏗᎦᎾᏄᎪᏫᏍᎩ ᎤᏰᎸᏒ ᏗᏕᏲᎲᏍᎩ ᎠᎭ. ᏌᏊ ᏗᏕᏲᎲᏍᎩ ᎡᎭ ᏂᎦᏛ ᏗᎦᎾᏄᎪᏫᏍᎩ ᎤᏂᏰᎸᏒ.
items.translator_confidence: very low; the whole point of this item is a subtle scope distinction that is hard enough to state in English, let alone Cherokee I'm not fluent in
items.label: unknown

items.english_source: No reptiles are warm-blooded. All snakes are reptiles. Question: No snakes are warm-blooded.
items.cherokee_candidate_translation: ᎥᏝ ᎦᎵᏍᎩᏂ ᎠᏫ ᎤᏗᏗᎦᎵᏍᏗ ᎨᏒ ᏱᎩ. ᏂᎦᏛ ᎢᎾᏅ ᎠᏫ ᎨᏐᎢ. ᎥᏝ ᎦᎵᏍᎩᏂ ᎢᎾᏅ ᎤᏗᏗᎦᎵᏍᏗ ᎨᏒ ᏱᎩ.
items.translator_confidence: very low
items.label: entailed

items.english_source: Noah is not happy. Question: Noah is sad.
items.cherokee_candidate_translation: ᏃᏩ ᎥᏝ ᎤᎵᎮᎵᏍᏗ ᏱᎩ. ᏃᏩ ᎤᏲᎢᏳ ᎦᏰᎸᏍᎦ.
items.translator_confidence: medium; short simple negation, closer to Week 1's easier items
items.label: unknown

items.english_source: Each brick in the wall is light. Question: The whole wall is light.
items.cherokee_candidate_translation: ᏂᎦᏓ ᏅᏯ ᎦᏍᎩᎶ ᎤᏓᏢᏗᏱ ᏗᎧᎵᎢ ᎨᏐᎢ. ᏂᎬ ᎦᏍᎩᎶ ᏗᎧᎵᎢ ᎨᏐᎢ.
items.translator_confidence: low
items.label: unknown

items.english_source: The committee is powerful. Question: Each member of the committee is powerful.
items.cherokee_candidate_translation: ᏗᎫᎪᏙᏗ ᎤᎵᏂᎩᏗᏳ ᎨᏐᎢ. ᏂᎦᏛ ᏗᎫᎪᏙᏗ ᎠᏂᎳᏫᎩ ᎠᏂᎵᏂᎩᏗᏳ.
items.translator_confidence: low
items.label: unknown

items.english_source: If the book says it is trustworthy, then it is trustworthy. The book says it is trustworthy. Question: The book is trustworthy.
items.cherokee_candidate_translation: ᎢᏳᏃ ᎪᏪᎵ ᎠᏗᎭ ᎤᏙᎯᏳᏗ ᎨᏐᎢ, ᎿᏉ ᎤᏙᎯᏳᏗ ᎨᏐᎢ. ᎪᏪᎵ ᎠᏗᎭ ᎤᏙᎯᏳᏗ ᎨᏐᎢ. ᎪᏪᎵ ᎤᏙᎯᏳᏗ ᎨᏐᎢ.
items.translator_confidence: low-medium; repeated predicate structure like this was one of the more reliable patterns in Week 1
items.label: entailed

items.english_source: The three swans Olivia saw were white. Question: All swans are white.
items.cherokee_candidate_translation: ᏦᎢ ᏥᏍᏆ ᎣᎵᏫᎠ ᎤᎪᎲᎯ ᎤᏁᎬ ᎨᏒᎩ. ᏂᎦᏛ ᏥᏍᏆ ᎤᏁᎬ ᎨᏐᎢ.
items.translator_confidence: low
items.label: unknown
